General.Description:
In 1713, a privateer captain known only as the Carpenter buried a fortune in silver and navigational instruments on an island that does not appear on any chart. He left behind a map — distributed across the spines of three different books, in a cipher he was certain no one would break because it required knowing a language no one who wasn't already dead still spoke.

Marine archaeologist Dr. Cass Devereux has been working on the cipher for nine years. She has finally broken it. The problem is that the three books — all rare, all extremely valuable in their own right — are currently in three different private collections. Two of the collectors are willing to cooperate. One, a reclusive shipping magnate with a reputation for solving his problems in ways that do not involve lawyers, very much is not.

The Bone Map is a gleefully paced treasure-hunt adventure that balances genuine historical research about the post-Spanish Succession Caribbean with fast, funny, and occasionally quite dangerous plot mechanics. Eliza Thornton writes her protagonist with warmth and wit — Cass is brilliant, stubborn, and perpetually underfunded — and the island setting is rendered with vivid, sun-bleached precision.

Enormously good fun.
